featured_reviews.review_text:
Dr. S. P. Mathew, who referred us to Dr. Manish Garg for my mother’s valve replacement surgery. Both doctors carry the values and legacy of KEM Hospital, and it is truly inspiring to see them serving society with such dedication.

Back in 1984, my mother underwent a kidney stone operation at KEM Hospital performed by Dr. Ravi Bapat. I have never personally met or seen Dr. Ravi Bapat, but the immense respect I have for him comes entirely from my mother’s words—her constant appreciation of his nature, expertise, and the way he handled her case. That itself speaks volumes about the kind of doctor he is.

Dr. Manish Garg performed my mother’s surgery exceptionally well. He was confident from the beginning, which gave us great reassurance. What truly stood out was his dedication—when my mother faced an emergency situation after surgery, he personally attended to her between 1 AM and 4 AM and handled everything remarkably well. I am sincerely grateful to him and his entire team.

He explains medical conditions very clearly, helping us understand the practical realities in advance. In today’s medical field, explaining difficult truths while respecting the patient’s emotions is a rare but essential quality—and something young doctors should learn from professionals like him.

The way Dr. Garg speaks with my mother itself brings her comfort and reduces half her suffering. Such empathy and human connection are extremely valuable in today’s time.

Just like the deep respect I developed for Dr. Ravi Bapat through my mother’s experience, I truly wish that Dr. Manish Garg achieves great success in his life and career. In today’s highly commercial medical environment, I believe he will prove himself as a distinct and rare gem—someone who not only treats symptoms but genuinely focuses on the root cause of the patient’s condition.

I extend my heartfelt gratitude and best wishes to Dr. Manish Garg. May he continue to serve people with the same dedication, compassion, and excellence.

I am giving a 5/5 rating so that people can understand in short, but honestly, for such a sensitive and dedicated doctor, even these ratings feel insufficient.

Thank you so much sir.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This has been one of the most disappointing medical experiences I’ve had. We visited this cardiologist for a second opinion, bringing along an angiography CD to assess the percentage of blockage and determine whether angioplasty was necessary or if medication could suffice.

Unfortunately, the doctor was unable to confidently read the CD. Initially, he said he wasn’t sure if there was any blockage at all (raising serious doubts about his expertise as a cardiologist). Then, within just 15 minutes, his diagnosis fluctuated from no blockage, to 30%, to 70%, and finally 70–80%. This inconsistency was alarming and did not inspire confidence.

He began the consultation by noting blood pressure, weight, and other basic vitals. While reviewing the case history and previously prescribed medications, he recommended discontinuing *Cortel-CH* (prescribed by another doctor), claiming it could cause headaches and flush sodium from the body. featured_reviews.name: Sunil Asnani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I cannot thank Dr. Mayur Jain enough for what he has done for my father and our family.

After my father underwent a mitral valve replacement surgery, he developed a clot within a year. We were extremely worried, especially when a very renowned cardiologist in Thane suggested that he would need to undergo another surgery so soon after the first one. The thought of putting him through another major operation within a year was terrifying for us.

Thankfully, we were guided to Jinkushal Hospital, where Dr. Mayur Jain carefully evaluated his condition. Instead of immediately recommending another surgery, he confidently advised treating the clot with proper medications and anticoagulants. He reassured us and chose a thoughtful, conservative approach rather than rushing into another procedure.

Within just six months, the 2D Echo report showed no clot. It felt nothing short of a miracle for our family.

Dr. Mayur Jain is not only an exceptional cardiologist but also a compassionate and honest human being who truly prioritizes his patients’ well-being. We feel incredibly fortunate that our family physician guided us to him.

To us, he is nothing less than God’s blessing.

Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Kami Dal Bahadur
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing first review on doctors and there is a lesson learnt so sharing my experience which was entirely unique and somewhat frightful.I took my father to the doctor for a cough and back pain, but the doctor never touched my father; instead, he spent much of his time on a laptop,finally he only spoke to him and instructed him to take an ECG..The doctor also told my father that he needed an angiogram test to determine the cause of the cough, prescribed two pills, and advised waiting a week or two in the hopes that the cough would go away.

But after a week, it didn't, so I thought to get a second opinion consulted a senior cardiologist who may be 40+ years of experience. He examined my father while he was lying down and checked thoroughly with a stethoscope. He said there was no need for any tests and that he was fine except for a cough for which he prescribed one medication, and for back pain, for which he advised consulting an orthopaedic specialist who may recommend an MRI scan.

After consulting with a senior orthopaedic doctor, he again examined my father and advised that he get an MRI for his spine. The MRI revealed that my father had spinal decompression and required surgery. If he had waited, his leg might not have felt anything, which is exactly what happened, but now my father has had the procedure. I did not hold off getting a second opinion for a week.

He explained me the findings of angiography after procedure and advised medications. Overall nice experience.
